why: Protocol 022 measured that fixed C keeps improving as the update budget grows (0.4256 -> 0.6891 PR-AUC over 100 -> 1600 updates, still +0.0323 at the tail), so an unconstrained online budget cannot support any statement about a capacity plateau.
S4 therefore runs under a deployment-plausible online budget, registered here BEFORE the run and not changed afterwards.

registered_online_process.loss: 0.7*detection CE + 0.3*resource CE + 0.5*ranking + 0.10*distillation(MSE to the frozen base detection logits) + 0.25*anchor(total)
registered_online_process.anchor_source: artifacts/ftmoe_online/protocol_020/adaptation_data/v1 train_indices[:24], rows 476..507 (the Protocol 020 R1 anchor pool)
registered_online_process.label_maturity: a label is usable only one interval after its own interval was observed (the settled index is strictly older than the read index)
registered_online_process.checkpoint_cadence: at every registered phase boundary (7 checkpoints)

implied_budget_per_phase.note: update opportunities are floor(scored_intervals / 4) with the opportunity taken on the last interval of each window of four; the realised counts are written to update_log.jsonl and must match this table

runtime_benchmark.required_by: directive §10 ('先做 runtime benchmark，把最终配置写入 online_budget.json')

measured.note: measured on the calibrated development stream with the frozen configuration above; the benchmark changed no parameter -- it only confirmed the run is affordable (a full 2880-interval arm is seconds of compute, so no budget compromise was needed)

runtime_benchmark.note: filled in by the benchmark run before the formal S4 start; the configuration above is not changed by it

forbidden_after_freeze: changing the update interval, the batch size or the number of gradient steps
changing the learning rate, the optimiser or the loss weights
